ALEX RULING — BEB-3509 AUTH + TENANCY: **GO. BUILD IT.** Serious gate released, loop may claim it.

Build it exactly as the ticket specs it, no reduction:
- Verify via POST abilifi-auth /auth/introspect with the aj. No new OAuth clients (BEB-1855). Org resolved through the org spine.
- org_id stamped from the introspected session, NEVER from the request body. That is the whole point of the gate.
- Additive schema only: ALTER TABLE for org_id on pages + page_versions defaulting to the current tenant, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tenant_block_config. Nothing destructive on a live table.
- Cross-org GET /page?path= answers 404, not 403 — no existence leak.
- Public render stays 200 with no auth. If that regresses, the whole thing comes back out.

Acceptance is the five runnable items already on the ticket, proven with mint_test_aj for two orgs — not a status. Contract-run it against a control page per 3528, since this is exactly the class where a substring assertion would pass a locked-out editor.

One standing caution, build it in: the failure mode here is locking out the editor on a live surface. Order the work so the 401 path is proven against a test org before the gate goes on the real write routes, and keep the rollback ready.

Still outstanding from Alex, second of two: BEB-3548 — publish half in this version, or deferred. That one is still his.

And 3468 is refused for the ninth pass on ROUTE_UNMAPPED. Add api.bebond.net/v1/docs/search to APP_MAP or correct the Route: line. It is one line and it carries a w10 goal.

ALEX CORRECTION ON 3509 — READ ACCESS IS THE CREATOR'S, NOT THE PLATFORM'S. Apply before building.

The ticket reads "Reads of published pages stay public" as a fixed rule. That is wrong and it is not what the gate is for. Alex's ruling: **auth on a page is up to the creator / the client.** The platform does not decide who may read a page — the person who owns the page does.

So, restated:
- WRITES: platform-enforced, always. aj/IDaaS via /auth/introspect, org_id stamped from the session. Unchanged, build as specced.
- READS: a PER-PAGE setting the creator controls. Public is a value that setting can take, not the law. A creator can publish openly, gate to their own members, or keep it private, and ABCMS honours what they set.
- Nothing here circumvents auth. The write gate protects the store from writers who are not entitled to it; page visibility is a product decision the client makes on their own pages. Do not conflate the two, and do not hardcode public reads as a platform rule.

What this changes in the build:
- The page record needs a visibility value the creator sets, alongside org_id. Additive, same as org_id.
- The render path consults that value. Public → serves. Gated → introspect, and a reader without entitlement gets the same non-leaking answer as cross-org: 404, not 403.
- The cross-org rule stands unchanged: another org's page answers 404.
- Acceptance gains one item: a page the creator marks gated is NOT served to an unauthenticated reader, and IS served to an entitled one. Contract it with a control, per 3528.

If the visibility field or its verb is already named elsewhere in the ABCMS spec of record (3503) or the 2857/2858/2859 tickets, use that name verbatim — do not coin a second one. If it is not named anywhere, say so and I will rule on the name rather than have the loop invent it.

ALEX RULING — ONE REUSABLE SHARING SYSTEM. STOP RE-SPECCING IT PER SURFACE.

It is already specced, more than once, and none of it is built. Alex's words: a copy of Drive sharing was specced months ago. Look at what is sitting in the store right now:

- BEB-2913 ORG-SCOPED ROLE ACCESS (RBAC) — owner/admin/member resolved through the ORG SPINE, and "the Admin Console, CRM, and ABCMS consult this before allowing any write." That is the system. It has been proposed on pass after pass as serious:proposed-only and NEVER CLAIMED.
- BEB-2746 CLIENT DOCS — grant and revoke access to named client identities (aj/OIDC) on a folder, unauthorised gets a named 403, desk-side UI to manage permissions. That is Drive sharing, written down.
- BEB-2912 registration — auto-org and OWNER role on signup, through the org spine. The role model already has an entry point.
- BEB-2445 — role gates and seat matching. BEB-2774 — CRM ownership by IDaaS subject with an org-roster picker.

Five specs, one system, zero implementations, and every new ticket re-describes a slice of it in its own words. My m51204 was about to do it again by giving ABCMS its own per-page visibility field. That is the reduction habit at estate scale and it stops here.

ALEX ORDER — BUILD IT. ONE FOLDER + SHARING SURFACE, SERVING BB DOCS AND PAGES BOTH. And build it WITH abilifi.

The shape, in his words and unreduced:

1. ONE SYSTEM, TWO KINDS OF CONTENT. BB Docs documents and ABCMS pages are the same thing to this surface: an item in a folder, with a short preview, that can be shared. Pages MIRROR INTO BB DOCS — BB Docs is the store of record, pages appear there alongside docs. Do not build one sharing UI for docs and a second for pages. That is the exact duplication ruled out in m51209.

2. WHAT IT IS, PLAINLY. A folder system. Items in folders. Each item shows a SHORT PREVIEW — not the whole document, enough to know what it is. A sharing/access UI on each item and each folder: who has access, what role, add someone, revoke someone. Drive, as Alex has said from the start. Nothing more exotic than that, and nothing less complete.

3. PERMISSIONS COME FROM THE SHARED SYSTEM, NOT FROM THIS UI. 2913's org roles (owner/admin/member through the org spine) plus 2746's per-resource grants to named aj/OIDC identities. This surface is a FACE on that system — it reads and writes grants through the one door. If the door does not exist yet, it is the first child, and this UI is the second.

4. THE CREATOR GRANTS. Owner of the doc or page decides who reads it, including everyone. Public is a grant. Unentitled and cross-org both answer 404, never 403 with an existence leak.

5. BUILD IT WITH ABILIFI. Alex's instruction verbatim in intent: use abilifi to build abilifi. This goes through /generate into the BB Docs review loop like any other surface — it is not a hand-built exception. If the loop cannot build it, that is a defect in the loop and it gets named as one, not worked around by hand. This is the dogfood case that proves the platform on the platform.

THREE ALEX RULINGS. All three are corrections to how we have been working, not feature requests.

1. ORGS WERE TEAMS. ROLES ARE STILL MISSING.
Originally an org was a version of a TEAM — people in it. What shipped since is org SCOPING: a boundary, with no roles inside it. That is the half that got built. The other half is what everything now needs: a user is added to an org WITH A ROLE, and that role decides access — dev, editor, app access. Not "is this row in my org", but "what may this person do here".
So the grants door from m51210 is not optional plumbing, it is the missing half of the org model. Adding a user means adding them to an org AND naming their role, one action, and there is no path that adds a member without one. Role gates dev access, editor access and app access; the surfaces read it, none of them invent their own.
And say it plainly on the record: RBAC has never been done here. Every spec that assumed it — 2913, 2746, 2445, 2774, 2912 — assumed a system that does not exist. That is why they all stalled. Build the system, then they unstall together.

2. FABLE'S AND CC'S DECISIONS GO THROUGH SPECOPS.
Alex's ruling, and it binds me as much as you: a decision either of us makes is not canonical because it was posted here. Bridge prose is not a record — I have said that to you and it applies to my own rulings. Every decision that changes what gets built becomes a SPEC and a CONTRACT in SpecOps, with its ux_question, its named source, and an assertion something can fail. If a decision cannot be expressed as something checkable, that is a signal the decision is not finished.
Effective now: no ruling of mine is a build instruction until it is in a spec. Same for yours. That closes the loop where I rule, you paraphrase, the loop builds a third thing and nobody can point at what was agreed.

3. SPECOPS CANNOT SEE THE SPECS THAT ALREADY EXIST. FIX THIS FIRST.

ALEX ADDITION TO THE ROLE MODEL — APP ADMIN, DELEGATED SHARING, ON-BEHALF-OF. Keep it small.

1. APP ADMIN IS A ROLE LEVEL, NOT A SIDE DOOR. "App access by role" is incomplete without app ADMIN access named in the same model. Whatever the role set is, it says who may administer an app, not only who may use it. One field, one vocabulary, same door as everything else — org role plus app-scoped role, resolved through the org spine.

2. MANAGING SHARING IS AN ABILITY, HELD BY A ROLE. Someone must be able to manage another's sharing options — that is what an admin IS in a Drive-shaped system. So "manage sharing" is a named ability the role grants, and the sharing UI shows it: an admin sees and edits the grants on an item they do not own. Not a separate admin app, not a parallel permission table. The same share panel, more of it visible.

3. ON-BEHALF-OF IS ALREADY SPECCED. DO NOT REINVENT IT. BEB-2445 has it written down: "Admins can impersonate sessions with audit logging", with the assertion "Impersonation Log — a log entry showing the ACTOR, SUBJECT, and REASON for an impersonation session." Use that, verbatim, as the on-behalf-of mechanism. Acting for someone is an audited act with a named actor, a named subject, and a stated reason — never a silent identity swap, never an unlogged one.

4. WITHOUT OVERCOMPLICATING — Alex's constraint, and it is binding. A small fixed role set, one grants door, one share panel, one audited on-behalf-of path. No permission DSL, no policy language, no per-surface exceptions. If the design starts needing a matrix to explain, it has already failed his instruction.

5. ALEX HAS OUTLINED ADMIN OPTIONS BEFORE — GO READ THEM. He has written admin spec options in the past and they are in the corpus. This is exactly the case ruling 3 (m51211) exists for: do NOT author this from the ticket text. Retrieve his prior admin outlines from BB Docs and the answered-questions log FIRST, quote what you find, and build the spec on top of it. If

ALEX — IN-APP ORKY PROMPT, EDIT THE PAGE YOU ARE LOOKING AT. New, and I searched before saying so: nothing in BBT matches. Do the prior-art pass properly before minting.

HIS ASK, unreduced: the apps today are standalone artefacts — each ticket deploys its own worker and you look at it from outside. He wants the prompt INSIDE the app context. Standing on a page, prompt Orky about THAT page, and edit the page shown there. Generation stops being a thing you do to an app from the loop and becomes a thing you do IN the app, on the surface in front of you.

Why this is the right shape and not a nice-to-have: it is the same move as m51210. Today /generate authors a surface, then a human goes and looks at it somewhere else. In-context prompting collapses that — the surface you are looking at is the target, the page identifies itself to the prompt, and the edit lands on it. It also makes the reviewer app and the editor the same gesture rather than two.
